1Panel-dev/laya-server.description: A self-hosted API and web interface for Laya's structured decision models, compatible with the TypeSafe Jev API format.
1Panel-dev/laya-server.body:
# Laya Server

A standalone Laya System One HTTP service and single-admin console. Backend uses FastAPI + SQLite, frontend uses React + Vite + TypeScript with shadcn/ui; after building, a single application container provides the web interface and API.

## Upstream Source

This repository does not track Laya source code. Before building, check out the pinned v0.3.7 version in the repository root:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya.git laya
git -C laya checkout --detach 010bacef009c855ccba814b51f7c8e1d38ab5e3f
sh scripts/check-upstream.sh
```

`laya/` has been added to `.gitignore`, but it will be included in the Docker build context. Dockerfile validates the complete SHA and a clean working directory; the final image contains only the upstream packages and licenses needed to run, excluding `.git`.

## Administrator and Configuration

Set `LAYA_ADMIN_USERNAME` and `LAYA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (at least 10 characters) in `.env`. The service will generate an Argon2id hash in memory at startup for login verification. Alternatively, you can skip the plaintext password and use `.venv/bin/python scripts/hash-password.py` to generate `LAYA_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH` instead; only one of these two must be set. Wrap the hash value in single quotes to ensure Docker Compose preserves the `$` literally. `LAYA_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` must also be configured; in production it must be an HTTPS origin, for example `https://console.example.com`. Local HTTP testing requires `LAYA_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCAL=1`. `.env` is already ignored by Git; do not commit actual passwords.

```sh
cp .env.example .env
python3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e 'backend[test]'
# Edit .env, fill in LAYA_ADMIN_USERNAME and LAYA_ADMIN_PASSWORD
```

## Model Files

Model weights are not distributed with the repository and image. `scripts/download-models.py` pins the Hugging Face repository to commit `1c5edc17a7acd8701df6fc341c0d179f1c62c982`, placing three checkpoints into the persistent model volume…

# Chapter 1\_Linux\_Kernel and Driver Learning Notes

This is a personal knowledge base for computer systems and Linux learning, with content covering fundamental theory, Linux common mechanisms, kernel subsystems, driver models, system software, platform implementations, experiments, projects, and source code research.

The Markdown files in the repository are the current form of notes and also material for future reformatting into Word/PDF. This emphasizes the structural sedimentation during the learning process, problem recording, and sustainable organization, without pursuing each article to be in final publication form from the start.

The repository adopts a layered information architecture of knowledge ontology, engineering applications, practical verification, research evidence, navigation arrangement, and repository governance. Knowledge text is stored only once, topics and learning paths organize links, experiments verify, and source code reading provides version evidence. The text maintains a unified reading sequence, publishing lists handle multi-document ordering and cross-document continuity; `markbook/` arranges the materials scattered in these responsibility layers of the same topic into monthly frozen, full-text searchable focused electronic books.

For the complete design, see: [Repository Information Architecture Design](https://github.com/FormingSystem/linux_note/blob/HEAD/governance/architecture/repository_information_architecture.md).

Each Markdown file contains `id`, `title`, `kind`, `status`, and `domains` metadata. `id` is used for long-term references, the main text continues to use unified section numbering to ensure reading positioning. You can use `./format.sh check all --summary` to simultaneously check titles, metadata, paths, and links.

## 1.1\_Repository Positioning

This repository unified manages computer system foundations, Linux common mechanisms, kernel subsystems, driver models, system software, platform implementations, experiments, projects, and source code research. Technical directions are organized through knowledge maps and learning paths, not through branch isolation of content.

Teaching examples and accompanying verification prioritize C/C++. Portable integers and container models run using standard compilers; Linux file operations, modules, and hardware experiments are marked with their target environments respectively, host model passing does not indicate the target experiment has been executed.

The remote repository is:

```text
https://github.com/FormingSystem/linux_note.git
```

| Directory | Content |

| `atlas/` | Knowledge maps, learning paths, indexes and roadmaps |
| `knowledge/` | Basic knowledge, Linux mechanisms, kernel subsystems, driver models and system software |
| `engineering/` | Engineering methods, building, porting, debugging, testing and release processes |

JennieCN/cityu-mail-pilot.description: Personalized real-time AI email processing software for Hong Kong City University, developed by INFE sophomore students
JennieCN/cityu-mail-pilot.body:
# CityU Mail Pilot

Convert emails from your school mailbox into a Chinese summary and send it back to you by email.

Your school mailbox is usually only accessible on a computer with Outlook open, which is inconvenient on your phone. This tool lets you **set up automatic forwarding in your CityU mailbox**, read emails from **your school** that are forwarded to your personal mailbox, generate a Chinese report using a large language model, and send it back to you — so you can see on your phone's email app **what this email requires you to do**.

**Read-only, only processes emails from your school. Use your own model key, or it can be uniformly provided by the person deploying this program.**

---

## How It Works

```
CityU Mailbox ──Auto Forward──▶ Your Personal Mailbox ──Read-only IMAP──▶ This Program ──▶ Chinese Report ──Email──▶ You
                                                                     │
                                                              Only retains @cityu.edu.hk emails
                                                              Generated using your (or this deployment's) API key
```

- **Read-only**: Throughout uses `BODY.PEEK[]`, never marks as read, never deletes, never modifies your emails
- **Only processes emails from your school**: Other emails are marked as "skipped" and written to the daily report, **will not be silently discarded**
- **Two key modes, billing follows the key**:
  - **Bring Your Own Key** (BYOK, default): Each account fills in their own key in "AI Model", model costs are paid directly to the provider, not through the deployer
  - **Uniformly provided by deployer**: Configure an instance-level key (`INFE_PILOT_DEFAULT_MODEL_KEY`, installation method see `docs/platform-key-2026-09-14.md`), **accounts without configured keys automatically use it**, billing is under the deployer's account. This is a **fallback, not an override** — if a user fills in their own key, their own key is still used. (**This repository's deployed instance works this way**: Before further notice, you don't need to configure your own key, it's uniformly provided by the deployer; if you self-host and don't configure a platform key, it reverts to the above — each person brings their own key.)
- **Reports are sent back by email**: No need to install an app, reports are right in your phone's email app

---

## What You Need

| | |
|---|---|
| A server | Ubuntu / Debian, SSH-accessible. Minimum 1 core 1 GB (this project's production environment is 2 cores 2 GB) |
| A personal mailbox | QQ / Gmail / 163 all work, needs IMAP enabled and **authorization code** generated (not login password) |
| A large language model API key | For example DeepSeek; **non-reasoning** models are recommended (see "Known Limitations" below) |
| A domain | ... |

# Take Your Playlist With You (PlaylistOut) ### 🎵 Cross-Platform Online Playlist Export and Backup Tool *Your playlists shouldn't be locked in a single music platform.* **🌐 [playlistout.lengxiqwq.com](https://playlistout.lengxiqwq.com)** 📖 README Language: Simplified Chinese · English

--- ## 💡 Why Build PlaylistOut (Take Your Playlist With You)? We've spent considerable time and effort organizing playlists on major music platforms, but often encounter such awkwardness: When wanting to switch platforms for listening, the old platform's playlists cannot be migrated directly; when wanting to back up your personal collections, there's nowhere to export song lists in a clean format; or simply wanting to organize songs into a spreadsheet for printing or statistical analysis, yet can only manually copy and paste one song at a time. The closed ecosystems of mainstream music platforms keep users' playlists tightly locked within a single app. **PlaylistOut (Take Your Playlist With You) has a simple goal: parse public playlists into structured data and return it to your hands.** - **Pure Client-Side Export**: All exported files are 100% generated in the user's browser local memory and triggered for download, never transmitted back to the server. - **Zero Barriers and Secure Authorization**: QQ Music and NetEase Cloud Music public playlists are 100% directly exported without login; Kugou Music supports free public preview without login, and can also use mobile app QR code scanning for secure authorization to unlock complete playlists (authorization credentials are only stored in the browser locally, the server has zero storage). No need to install any extensions or client software. - **Focused and Pure**: It is not a player, does not download audio files, nor perform redundant cloud synchronization; it focuses solely, stably, and completely on solving the single task of "playlist data export, backup, and migration". --- ## 🚀 Online Usage No need to install any software, just open **[playlistout.lengxiqwq.com](https://playlistout.lengxiqwq.com)** to get started: 1. **Paste Playlist** — Supports links from QQ Music, NetEase Cloud Music, Kugou Music, and Soda Music platforms (web links, mobile short links, pure playlist IDs, or app-shared content with text, automatically extracted by the system). You can also directly load all public playlists from a user by entering their homepage link or numeric ID. 2. **Real-Time Parsing** — Edge Workers automatically parse playlist metadata, song names, artists, albums, cover art, and VIP/delisted availability status. 3. **Complete Preview** — Check the complete song list, total track count, and song status directly on the webpage before exporting. 4. **One-Click Export / Copy** — Save locally as TXT / CSV / Excel (.xlsx) / JSON, or directly copy to clipboard with one click; support batch packing multiple playlists into multi-sheet workbooks or ZIP archives. --- ## ✨ Main Features ### 🔗…

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
```

boatraceopenapi/api.body:
⚠️ Caution

**Please confirm the following before using this API.**

- **It is unofficial.** It has no relation with the official BOATRACE website and related organizations.
- **It is not real-time.** Due to regular updates at approximately 3-minute intervals via GitHub Actions, there may be a delay of several minutes in reflecting the latest information.
- **We do not guarantee accuracy or completeness.** Due to collection and conversion, there may be missing or incorrect data.
- **If you need official information, please check the official BOATRACE website.**
- **Use at your own risk.**

---

📝 Overview

With this API, you can retrieve boatrace (motorboat racing) data. The data is published on GitHub Pages and provided in JSON format.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Supported race venues | All 24 venues nationwide (data for one day includes information from all venues) |
| Available data | Starting lineups, last-minute information, results |

---

🌐 Endpoints

Supported period: **From January 1, 2026 onwards**

```bash
https://boatraceopenapi.github.io/api/v1/YYYY/YYYYMMDD.json
```

- `YYYY` → Year
- `YYYYMMDD` → Year, month, date
- Dates are based on Japan Standard Time (JST / UTC+9)

> If you specify a date for which data does not exist (outside the supported period, future dates, etc.), HTTP 404 will be returned due to GitHub Pages specifications.

---

📦 Response Specification

For details on the JSON structure of the response and each field, refer to the schema documentation.

→ [docs/v1/schema.md](https://github.com/boatraceopenapi/api/blob/HEAD/docs/v1/schema.md)

💡 Examples

dataelement/dsh-site-selection.body:
# Store Location Selection Workbench

**Simplified Chinese** | [English](https://github.com/dataelement/dsh-site-selection/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

DSH (DeepSeek Harness) Plugin. **Point to any location on a real 3D city map and instantly get site selection analysis for that point**——
Tell your requirements to DSH in plain language, it batch finds locations based on the same model and writes them into a list; once you like a location, collect rental properties available there; after site visits, fill back in feedback, and the chat on the right can understand which location you selected throughout the process.

## Features

- **Click Anywhere to Analyze** — Millisecond-level analysis for any location on the map: scores across three dimensions, percentile for each metric, risk alerts, customer demographic composition
- **Score by Business Type** — Opening a coffee shop vs. a pharmacy yields different scores at the same location: based on the distribution of existing stores of the same business type in the city as a baseline
- **Find Locations in Plain Language** — "Within 200m of metro, plenty of restaurants, no more than 3 similar shops, find 10 locations", DSH translates into queries and runs the same data
- **Two-level List: Location → Property Source** — First assess if a location is viable, then see what properties are available to rent there. Collected property sources automatically link to the nearest location, using their own tan/brown color on the map, list, and details, not confused with locations
- **Property Source Layer** — One-click overlay rental property sources on the map, labels show rent (RMB/㎡/day); click location details to auto-list properties within 400m
- **Candidate List** — All location metrics side-by-side, sorted by score, click rows to locate on the map
- **3D City Base Map** — Real road networks, land use, building outlines and heights, self-drawn canvas, no tiles, no API key, runs offline
- **Site Visit Loop** — To see → Visited → In meeting → Signed/Declined, advance each step with one click in the list; decisions are recorded and can be reverted
- **Change City with One Command** — `fetch-city.mjs` builds the dataset, restart and you're ready to go, no code changes

## Desktop Workbench Adaptation (1.2.0)

Requires DSH Desktop that provides `desktopWorkbenches.register`, `isActive`, and `ownsSession`. After installing the provider plugin, add and open "Store Location Selection" in "Workbench Market", the entry is fixed, repository identity and session ownership are managed by Desktop. flypigJ/Tailscale-OHOS.body:
# MeshArc

A Tailscale community client built for HarmonyOS NEXT, connecting devices, transferring files, and accessing remote storage and media services.

---

After going out, access the NAS at home, send files from your phone to your computer, or open a remote media library. MeshArc brings these common operations into the HarmonyOS native interface, allowing your HarmonyOS device to join an existing Tailscale network (tailnet).

**MeshArc is an independent community project and not an official Tailscale client.** This repository retains the `Tailscale-OHOS` name, with the app name being MeshArc.

## One Connection, Endless Possibilities

| What You Want to Do | Capabilities MeshArc Provides |
| --- | --- |
| **Access Your Own Devices** | Log in to Tailscale, view device online status, connection paths and latency, and access remote services via Tailscale IP. |
| **Use Home or Remote Networks** | Select available exit nodes, receive approved subnet routes, and configure local network access when using exit nodes. |
| **Transfer Files Between Devices** | MeshSend integrates Taildrop send/receive and provides LocalSend service integration entry; supports transfer progress, cancellation, retry, and received file management. |
| **Browse Remote Files** | Access shared and authorized directories in Taildrive, browse files and upload/download; available operations depend on sharing permissions. |
| **Open Remote Media Libraries** | Detect Jellyfin, Emby, and Plex services, and pass server information to HosPlayer; media accounts are logged in within the player. |
| **Enjoy Native HarmonyOS Experience** | Native ArkUI interface, Chinese and English, light and dark themes, and adaptive layouts for phones, tablets, and 2-in-1 devices. |

Feature descriptions are based on the publicly available source code in this repository; versions in app stores, development branches, and historical installation packages may differ, please refer to the update log of the version you have installed.

## Getting Started

### 1. Get MeshArc

**[Go to Huawei AppGallery →](https://appgallery.huawei.com/app/detail?id=io.github.tailscaleohos)**

Please confirm in the app store whether your device supports installation. The baseline for the source code project is **HarmonyOS 6.1 / API 23, arm64**; the specific system requirements for the version in the app store should be confirmed in the app store.

## Project Introduction

ImQi1 CMS is a full-stack personal blog and content management system built with **Nuxt 4 + Prisma + TailwindCSS**, and is also the complete source code of the personal site [imqi1.com](https://imqi1.com). It is not a generic CMS template, but rather a one-stop content platform tailored around the positioning of "technology sharer, life photographer, current affairs commentator", covering the complete workflow from content creation, publishing, management to multi-platform display.

The project adopts an **SSR + ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration)** architecture: pages are rendered on the server to ensure first-screen performance and SEO, while leveraging Redis cache to store rendering results (when Redis is not configured, pages are not cached as a whole and are rendered in real-time each time, and search caching is turned off), balancing performance and real-time updates — ISR routes uniformly expire after **30 minutes** (the duration is controlled by the `ISR_CACHE_SECONDS` constant in `nuxt.config.ts`, content changes are visible site-wide within 30 minutes at the latest). The data layer uses Prisma 7 with PostgreSQL adapter to directly connect to PG, and front-end and back-end types are automatically inferred through Nuxt's `InternalApi`, eliminating the need for additional type generators.

In addition to the main web site, the repository also includes a mini-program end based on **uni-app** as a Git submodule (`mini/`), supporting H5 / WeChat mini program / Alipay mini program across three platforms, and reuses the dedicated API provided by the main site.

Main capabilities include:

- **Content Creation**: Complete Markdown writing experience, code highlighting based on Shiki, and support for extended syntax and rich media such as container alerts, emojis, image lightbox, and live photos (LivePhoto).
- **Content Organization**: Articles, standalone pages, categories and tags (polymorphic meta), article archives, changelogs, and site search.

liuyangyi0/kungfukid-local-server.body:
# KungFuKid Local Server

Self-built Python/SQLite local compatibility service and Windows client adapter source code.

New `--mode public` feature enables invitation-code-based registration for non-ranked public testing: targets 100 accounts, 8 players per room, with server-side authentication, encryption, permissions, and resource limits; no VM, specific DLL, PID, or client firewall dependencies. The default example still listens on loopback; this release has no production-grade security authentication or deployment configuration.
See [Service Specification](https://github.com/liuyangyi0/kungfukid-local-server/blob/HEAD/docs/SERVICE.md) for third-party standard integration, and [server/deploy](https://github.com/liuyangyi0/kungfukid-local-server/blob/HEAD/server/deploy/README.md) for operations templates. Complex battle sub-protocols and permanent battle rewards are disabled by default and cannot guarantee complete anti-cheat or full original client compatibility.

This is an experimental project in development, **not a complete game distribution package or a fully protocol-recovered legacy server**. It does not include the original client, game assets, account databases, IDA/PDB, packet captures, memory dumps, user credentials, or authentication private keys. The source code contains only fixed compatibility constants needed to parse existing file and frame formats, not legacy server private keys. Users must provide their own authorized clients and test in isolated environments.

- `client-adapter/reference-scripts/`: Original experiment host/client startup templates for reference only; cannot be directly used on arbitrary computers.
- `docs/CLIENT_COMPATIBILITY.md`: Client adaptation methods, prerequisites, and migration steps.
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT_WALKTHROUGH.md`: Step-by-step procedures from directory layout through dependencies, compilation, accounts, service, public keys, loading, and validation.
- `docs/AI_PROTOCOL_WORKFLOW.md`: Reusable AI collaboration protocol recovery and testing workflow.
- `client-adapter/tools/`: Read-only PE/public key verification and local account creation tools with hidden password input.

webkubor/dsh-llm-hub.body:
·  English · Changelog

DSH's model page is missing half of what the official adapter should do. This plugin fills in the gap: | | Official Adapter | dsh-llm-hub | |---|---|---| | What models does DeepSeek have | Can't see | **One-click fetch available models** | | How much balance is left in account | Can't see | **Balance card + threshold alert** | | Whether gateway works and how fast | Button click has no response | **Actual latency and status + health dashboard** | | How many models on the gateway | Can't see | **Tested: 71 models** (manual entry only has 11) | | Why detection fails | No hint | **Clearly states 'baseURL not configured'** | | How many tokens spent this month | Not available | **Usage statistics + top 5 most-used models + CSV export** | | Unavailable providers still in dropdown | Still appears | **Silently removed from dropdown, marked red on card + reason** | | External agent CLI (codex/claude/agy) | Regardless of install, no impact | **If installed, sub-agent tools appear** |
After installation, the model page: each provider card has an additional line below — protocol, access address, number of configured models, balance, with probe and fetch directory on the right

## Installation ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-plugins/dsh-llm-hub ``` Then add `@dsh-plugins/dsh-llm-hub` to the `dsh.profile.bundles` array in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`, then `~/.dsh/restart.sh`. Open **Settings → Models**, and an additional line will appear below the provider card. Boot graph changes require restart, hot reload won't work; `cordis.patch.yml` is automatically inserted by the bundle mechanism. --- ## What does it fill in DSH already has all the mechanisms in place, what's missing is "the official adapter doesn't use them": | Capability | Official Mechanism | Official Direct Connection Current State | |---|---|---| | Model Discovery | `registerModelDiscovery(ns, discover)` from `llm` service + "Get Available Models" on Models page | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek` **never registered** (tested in versions `0.1.2-rc.1` and `0.1.5-rc.2`, `discover` returned zero hits in both)…
